entries.title: ZAP
entries.body: Bitcoin micropayment made via the Lightning Network and cryptographically linked to a Nostr event. Defined by NIP-57, the zap mechanism allows a user to directly reward the author of a post by sending satoshis from their Lightning wallet. Zaps are one of the most successful integrations between Bitcoin and Nostr, enabling a direct compensation model, with no intermediary and no possibility of censorship.

entries.title: ZBD
entries.body: Company founded in 2019 specializing in integrating Lightning payments into the video game industry. Formerly known as Zebedee, it provides APIs and SDKs that allow game developers to integrate transactions in sats and that give players the ability to earn and spend real bitcoins in virtual worlds. ZBD also offers a mobile application that acts as a Lightning wallet dedicated to gaming, as well as a streaming payments infrastructure.

entries.title: ZEROCONF
entries.body: Risky practice of considering a Bitcoin transaction as final, and proceeding to carry out the associated counterpart action (such as the sale of a good or service), before the transaction is actually included in a block on the blockchain. Unconfirmed, or zeroconf, transactions are vulnerable to double-spend attacks, because they are not yet irrevocably recorded in the ledger. Zeroconf may possibly be considered in very specific contexts, where speed is the priority, such as in the case of small commercial transactions or in the case of a transaction between relatives or close friends. In these situations, the risk of double spending is often considered acceptable compared to the advantage of a fast transaction. Nevertheless, for large transactions, especially when the sender is unknown, it is crucial to wait for several confirmations before considering the transaction immutable. The generally accepted standard is to wait for 6 confirmations, which means that 5 additional blocks must be mined after the one including the transaction, in order to consider it final.

entries.title: ZEROLINK
entries.body: Chaumian coinjoin protocol that aims to break all links between sets of separate coins through advanced mixing techniques. The ZeroLink protocol stands out for its ability to protect users' anonymity against various forms of chain analysis at the transaction and network level. ZeroLink introduces a framework for coinjoin wallets, with the use of segregated pre-mix and post-mix accounts, as well as a mixing technique of its own: the Chaumian coinjoin. The two main implementations of ZeroLink have been Wasabi Wallet (version 1.0) and Whirlpool, available on Samourai Wallet and Sparrow Wallet. This protocol [was introduced by nopara73 and TDevD in 2017](https://github.com/nopara73/ZeroLink/blob/master/README.md).

entries.title: ZEROSYNC
entries.body: Project developed to take advantage of ZKPs (zero-knowledge proofs) in the Bitcoin ecosystem, in order to improve the scalability and privacy of the system. Their main protocol (also named *ZeroSync*) makes it possible to compress the history of the Bitcoin blockchain, in order to speed up the initial synchronization of nodes with the network through the use of a compact proof, without compromising verification.

entries.title: ZEUS
entries.body: Open source mobile application that allows managing a Lightning Network node from a phone. Zeus can operate in two modes: remote connection to an existing Lightning node (LND, Core Lightning or Eclair), or use of a Lightning node integrated directly into the application thanks to an embedded LND implementation. Zeus makes it possible to send and receive Lightning and on-chain payments, manage one's payment channels, view the status of one's node and configure routing fees.

entries.title: ZKP - ZERO-KNOWLEDGE PROOF
frenchAliases: PREUVE À DIVULGATION NULLE DE CONNAISSANCE
entries.body: Cryptographic method allowing one party (the prover) to prove to another party (the verifier) that a piece of information is true, without revealing the information or any aspect of it. A ZKP makes it possible to guarantee the accuracy of a statement, while preserving the confidentiality of the underlying data.

entries.title: ZKSNACKS
entries.body: Company that publishes Wasabi Wallet, an open source desktop Bitcoin wallet focused on privacy. zkSNACKs developed the WabiSabi protocol, a coinjoin mechanism used in Wasabi Wallet 2.0 to improve the privacy of Bitcoin transactions. In June 2024, zkSNACKs ended its coinjoin coordination service due to regulatory uncertainty. Wasabi Wallet continues to operate as a standard Bitcoin wallet, and other WabiSabi coinjoin coordinators have emerged.

entries.title: ZMQ - ZEROMQ
entries.body: Asynchronous messaging library used by Bitcoin Core to notify other software in real time of the arrival of new blocks and new transactions. ZMQ operates on a publish-subscribe model (*pub/sub*): Bitcoin Core publishes events on a socket, and subscribed software (such as LND) receives them instantly without having to periodically poll the node. This interface is essential for Lightning implementations that must react quickly to transaction confirmations, notably for detecting channel closures and broadcasting justice transactions.

entries.title: ZOMBIE CHANNEL
entries.body: Lightning channel considered inactive, generally because the remote peer has suffered a failure or has not been online for a prolonged period. A *zombie channel* ties up capital without being usable to route payments, which reduces the node operator's available liquidity. This type of channel can also be problematic when attempting to recover a Lightning node via an SCB (*Static Channel Backup*). It is recommended to close these channels when it becomes unlikely that the peer will come back online.

entries.title: ZPRV
entries.body: Extended private key prefix for SegWit V0 accounts on Bitcoin.

entries.title: ZPUB
entries.body: Extended public key prefix for SegWit V0 accounts on Bitcoin.
